```{r}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(222)
theme_set(theme_bw())
```

Here we'll verify our understanding of a statisticsal procedure using simulation.

## 1. Choose the parameters for our simulation

```{r}
p1 <- 0.60
n1 <- 35
p2 <- 0.52
n2 <- 25
```

## 2 Simulate a sample and calculate the sample statistic

Use `rbinom()` for our binary response variable (Soil Pb > 200).

```{r}
pre1950 <- rbinom(n = 1, size = n1, prob =p1)
post1950 <- rbinom(n = 1, size = n2, prob =p2)

# Our sample statistic

phat1 <- pre1950 / n1
phat2 <- post1950 / n2
diff_prop <- phat1 - phat2
```

## 3. Coninue simulating samples until we reach critical mass

In this case, lets do 10,000...

```{r}
pre1950 <- rbinom(n = 1e4, size = n1, prob = p1)
post1950 <- rbinom(n = 1e4, size = n2, prob = p2)

phat1 <- pre1950 / n1
phat2 <- post1950 / n2
diff_prop <- phat1 - phat2

tibble(diff_prop) |> 
    ggplot(aes(diff_prop)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.04) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = p1 - p2, color = "cornflowerblue", linewidth = 1.2)
```

Looks pretty normal!

## 4. Check our simulation results against the claim

>95% of samples tats fall within 1.96 SEs (standard errors) of the population pararmeter.

```{r}
se <- sqrt(phat1 * (1 - phat1) / n1 + phat2 * (1 - phat2) / n2)
head(se)

mean((p1 - p2 >= diff_prop - 1.96 * se) & (p1 - p2 <= diff_prop + 1.96 * se))
# What fraction of the time was true pop prop greater than our diff in SEs
# How often is it falling within 1.96 SEs
```

Good but not perfect! Coverage is 93.8%, whihc is a bit under the expected 95%

Think about...
1. What do you think might be affecting the accuracy of this inference?
2. Once you come up with a hypothesis, how would you modify this experiement to test your hypothesis?
